newsitem.title: USA: S.F. Fed study suggests inflation targets useful.
newsitem.headline: S.F. Fed study suggests inflation targets useful.

text.p: Inflation targets appear to have resulted in a more favorable price picture in a handful of countries that have adopted the targets, according to an economist with the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco.

However, it may take time before the benefits of the strategy are fully reflected in the behavior of long-term interest rates, economist Chan Huh wrote in the latest issue of the San Francisco Fed's weekly Economic Letter.
Huh looked at the experiences of several countries, such as New Zealand, Canada and Britain, whose central banks have been using inflation targets. He focused in particular on Britain.
"In most countries mentioned in this Letter, inflation in the targeted price indexes has remained within the target range in the past year or so," he said.
He added that, on average, inflation was lower in major industrial countries using the targets than it was in those that were not.
Still, a country's track record played an important role in determining confidence in the central bank's commitment to maintaining low inflation.

Huh pointed out that the inflation risk premium built into long-term German interest rates is relatively low, even though the Bundesbank does not use inflation targets. The low risk premium reflects the Bundesbank's long-standing reputation for vigilance against inflation.
In Britain, long-term rates have fallen relative to German rates but the differential continues to favor Germany.

"It appears that while (inflation-targeting) has helped gain credibility for U.K. monetary policy, the markets are not yet fully convinced that policy will stick with its current stringent (targeting) approach in the long run," Huh said.
Huh said this showed how difficult it was to establish credibility in monetary policy.
"While institutional changes may enhance credibility, it will take years of solid performance to earn the public's full belief in the central bank's commitment to low inflation," Huh concluded.
